newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Jagland says may sell more bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Jagland says may sell more bank shares.

text.p: Norway's new prime minister Thorbjoern Jagland said on Friday the government may reduce its controlling stake in the country's top commercial banks to below 50 percent.
"I am no supporter of selling off the state's share in the private banks but two goals dictate how much the state should keep," Jagland told his first news conference after taking office.

The new premier, who is seen to stand to the left of former premier Gro Harlem Brundtland, is an advocate of continued state ownership of key industries and the top commercial banks Den Norske Bank ASA (DNB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA.
"One (goal) is to maintain national ownership and the other to have a stable ownership and control of these banks. If you need 33 percent or 50 percent is not important," he said.
Asked if the government could see itself reducing its stake belowe 50 percent in Jagland said:
"Yes, but we have not taken a position on it. We have only said we don't want to sell ourselves below 50 percent in this legislature and we will see what happens in the next period."
Norway holds elections in September next year.
Jagland's predecessor, Gro Harlem Brundtland, said last March the government should eventually cut its stake in the country's top commercial banks to below 50 percent.
The State Bank Investment Fund (SBIF) in June completed the sale of 19 percent of shares in DnB, reducing the state-held stake to 52 percent.
Earlier, the state cut its stake in Christiania to 51 percent from 69.
The state was left holding majority stakes in DnB, Christiania and other top banks after rescuing them from a financial crisis in 1988-92.
The government has sold off its shares in Union Bank of Norway and Fokus Bank but has said it wants to retain control of DnB and Christiania for strategic national reasons.
The government pumped 14.76 billion norwegian crowns ($2.3 billion) into DnB, Christiania and Fokus to bail them out.
All have since returned to profit, buoyed by a stronger economy and huge net reversals on loan losses.
But Norwegian industry, which fears state ownership might skew competition, has repeatedly called on the government to sell its stake and cede control of the banks. ($ = 6.457 Norwegian Crowns)
